address.plainHttp: Plain http is accepted only for localhost, and only when the person who runs this server has set {{env}}=true. For any other address use https.
address.privateBlocked: This server only talks to public addresses. To use a model on your own machine or network, the person who runs this server sets {{env}}=true and restarts it. In Docker, localhost is the container itself, and plain http is accepted only for localhost, so a model on the host machine needs an https address this server can reach (or the server run outside Docker).

flag.bannedTerm: Uses a word you ruled out
form.baseUrl: Start with https:// (or http:// for a model on this machine). No name, password or key in the address.
form.budget: Use a whole number from 0 to {{max}}. 0 means no limit here.
form.costCap: Use an amount in dollars, such as 25. 0 means no cap.
form.model: Use the model name exactly as your provider gives it, with no spaces.
form.priceIn: Use an amount in dollars, such as 3 or 0.25.
form.priceOut: Use an amount in dollars, such as 15 or 0.6.
form.softWarn: Use a whole number from 0 to 100. 0 means no warning.
hint.noText: The model sent no text. Some servers put the answer elsewhere when a model thinks first.
hint.notJson: The model did not answer with JSON. Models that think first, or small models, often do not: try a model made for structured answers, or turn thinking off.
hint.schema: The answer did not have the shape the task needs. A larger or instruction-tuned model usually fixes that.
hint.truncated: The answer was cut off before it ended. A very small model can ramble past the limit, and one that thinks first can use it up: try a larger instruct model.
